The Button Behind the Message

消息背后的按钮 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A library introduced an online account for its reading service. A patron named Dani received a message asking her to renew a subscription that was not due. It carried the library logo and an accurate price. The payment button led to an unfamiliar website. She opened the library's usual homepage on a desktop computer and saw no bill. At the help desk she showed a librarian both pages. The message looked official enough to deceive someone who had only a smartphone and a minute to spare.

2The librarian checked the account database. Nobody had added a payment request. A second reader had received similar spam through a mobile application. A fake dialog asked for a username and a debit card number. A technician examined the URL without downloading an attachment. On a plain notepad he saw one erroneous letter. The dishonest webpage had cloned an old registration form, including its font, toolbar, and cursor. It looked up-to-date enough to pass a quick check on a cell-phone.

3They checked what the scam actually knew. A public spreadsheet column had listed readers at an event. A hacker could exploit that limited information. It included no confidential profile, but the corresponding names could be copied into an inbox. The technician reviewed network tracking and compared a backup on disk. The two databases still matched. The library could circulate a warning without accusing someone of a virus or an intrusion. It also deleted an outdated download that made the fake invitation look more convincing.

4A volunteer wanted to publicize a screenshot of the deceptive message. The technician hid the live link. A handout and slideshow showed how to open the homepage, scroll to a renewal date, and log out afterward. A barcode led to the same page on the official site. Readers without internet could ask at the desk. One patron used a tablet and its touchpad to test the directions. Another made a printout for her neighbor. The library added a voicemail message to summarize the change.

5One flaw remained. A browser extension could block the genuine renewal screen. The programmer checked its compatibility with a compact tablet. He added an account summary before payment and an offline mode for the desk. Staff could check expiry dates while a wireless router needed a reboot. An employee proposed automating the warning with a popup. They kept a quieter version in the toolbar, where a reader could choose to refresh the page without clicking a strange link.

6They also reviewed the old website. Its registration link ran through a commercial client. A support worker had left a classified document in a shared folder after it expired. This was a separate glitch, but it showed how easily staff could expose information electronically. A librarian proposed tracking usage before enabling another interactive feature. The technician disconnected an obsolete cable, checked the remaining access licenses, and asked staff to communicate one rule on the web and at the desk.

7At the next class a reader asked whether fingerprint login or a webcam could stop the fraud. The technician said it could protect a device but could not identify a dishonest webpage. Dani demonstrated how to close a false dialog, erase a misleading bookmark, and use the official address again. One person had to uninstall a browser extension. Another asked why a useful printer adaptor looked like a network gadget. A picture on the handout made the hardware easier to identify without plugging anything into an unfamiliar socket.

8Two months later Dani checked the catalog, then renewed at the desk. A teller from a bank happened to be there. He knew how contactless payment worked but found the library's keyboard unfamiliar. Dani let him browse the genuine page and showed where to check copyright and license details. A ringtone interrupted them. The visitor ignored it. An annoying message could wait while he completed a transaction on a trustworthy page.

四级汇总词汇 · 11中文译文

消息背后的按钮

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1图书馆推出了网上读者账户。读者达妮收到一条续订提醒，可她的服务还没到期。消息带着图书馆的标志，价格也对，付款按钮却通向一个陌生网站。她用台式机打开平时进的主页，账户里没有账单。她去服务台给馆员看了两个页面。消息足够像官方通知，只有一部手机、又来不及细看的人很可能受骗。

2馆员查了账户数据库，没人添加付款请求。第二位读者也在手机应用里收到类似垃圾消息，假对话框让他填用户名和借记卡号码。技术员没下附件，先把网址抄到记事本，找出一个错字母。假网页复制了旧注册表，包括字体、工具栏和光标。在手机上匆匆看一眼，很容易以为它是现用页面。

3他们检查骗子究竟知道什么。一个公开表格曾列出活动的参与者。黑客可以利用这些有限资料，把对应的名字复制进邮件，却没见到任何保密账户资料。技术员核对网络记录和磁盘备份，两个数据库仍然一致。图书馆可以发出警告，无须先断定有病毒或入侵。他们还删掉一个过时的下载件，免得假通知借它显得更可信。

4一位志愿者想公开诈骗截图。技术员先遮住能点开的链接。传单和简短演示教读者怎样从主页找到续订日期，用完再退出。条形码也指向官网同一页。没网的人可以来服务台。一位读者用平板和触控板试了流程，另一人给邻居打了一份。图书馆还在语音信箱里简要说明了改变。

5正式系统还有个缺陷。浏览器扩展可能拦住真正的续订页。程序员用一台小平板测试兼容性，在付款前加了账户摘要，也给服务台做了离线模式。无线路由器重启时，工作人员仍能查到期日期。有人提议用弹窗自动提醒。他们把提示留在工具栏，读者可以自己刷新页面，无须点击陌生链接。

6他们也检查了旧网站。注册入口经由一个商业客户端。有人把已失效的机密文件留在共享文件夹里。这是另一个故障，却说明电子资料多么容易被无意公开。馆员提议先了解使用情况，再开新互动功能。技术员断开旧线缆，核对还有效的访问许可，请工作人员在网上和服务台讲同一条规则。

7下一堂课，有人问指纹登录或摄像头能不能挡住诈骗。技术员说，这些能保护设备，却不能辨出假网页。达妮示范怎样关掉假对话框，删掉误导书签，再用正式地址进入。有人卸载了浏览器扩展。另一人问，为什么打印机转接器看着像网络设备。传单上的图让人不用插进陌生插口也能认出它。

8两个月后，达妮自己查过目录，在服务台续订。旁边恰好有位银行柜员。他熟悉非接触式付款，却不习惯馆里的键盘。达妮让他浏览真正的页面，指给他看版权和许可信息。铃声打断了他们，来客没理会。烦人的消息可以等，眼下他正在可信页面完成交易。
